editorial:
Imagine the chaos that happens when the clumsiest guy in the world decides to get a puppy. You get to follow Goofy as he brings home a cute little dog named Bowser, thinking it will be a breeze to raise him. The vibe is light and silly, focusing on the funny struggle of trying to train a pet that just won't listen. It feels like a classic cartoon sketch where everything that can go wrong definitely does, making it a great pick for a quick laugh when you just want to relax.

What really works here is the physical comedy and the way Bowser grows at a scary speed. The pacing is quick, so you never get bored watching the neighbors get more and more annoyed with the giant dog. While it is a short film and not a full-length feature, the humor still hits home. If you enjoy old-school Disney charms, you should definitely check this out. You can easily find this while streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Disney Plus or by adding the physical Blu-ray to your collection for a movie night with the kids.
endingExplained: The story wraps up when Goofy leaves Bowser home alone to act as a guard dog. Bowser is way too friendly and lets everyone in, but the moment Goofy actually returns, Bowser treats him like a total stranger. The dog ends up attacking his own owner in a funny way because he finally thinks he is doing his job. It ends with Goofy learning that training a dog is much harder than it looks.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic Disney cartoons and goofy pets.
